what_was_asked: Every skirmish and multiplayer map must show a good-looking asteroid field made of many small rocks, so a mining station can be placed and built on it.

what_changed.prop: one irregular boulder (displaced icosphere, 320 triangles, stone roles base/dark/trim) replacing four overlapping bevelled boxes with faction hardware roles
what_changed.draw: 64 small rocks per field, area-weighted scatter held inside the field radius, instead of one instance of the prop scaled up to the radius
what_changed.envelope: unchanged at +-0.58 X/Z and +-0.46 Y, so ASTEROID_EXTENT and every projected size hold

asteroid-field-comparison.png.shows: 2x2 sheet: the same field in the same native frame before and after, wide and close

native-field-verification.json.shows: a measurement of the same revision in the real skirmish frame (see limits below)

what_the_measurement_does: renders the whole scene the production collector builds for skirmish01 (ships, planets, stations, 320 rocks) through the native viewer
renders the same frame again with only the aimed-at field removed, so occlusion by every other object cancels out

drops the sparse silhouette/starfield flicker between the two renders (dense mask), then measures the footprint against the projection: centre error, span ratio, share of the disc that is rock, and whether the field reaches the frame edge
result on this revision: passed=True, centre_error=[0.014, 0.014], size_ratio=[0.86, 0.75], disc_fill=0.147, fields_drawn=5, rock_instances=320

controls.note: the clipped bounding box still reads as correctly sized, which is why the disc fill and the frame-edge check exist

controls.sabotage: field shifted by 0.8 of its radius
one boulder at 0.95 of the radius instead of a scatter
the earlier flaky measurement (raw difference, no dense mask)
controls.expected: fail on ~1 run in 4 with no code change
controls.observed: 6 of 27 runs failed; with the dense mask 4 of 4 runs agree to the digit

limits: This measures a footprint, not beauty. The appearance was approved by the owner looking at the sheet and the two captures; the numbers here cannot approve a picture.
It proves one map (skirmish01) and one field. The unit tests cover the other maps, the live emitter and the rock scatter; the pixel proof does not.
A field drawn in the right place at the right size with ugly rocks would pass. That is what the sheet is for.
